sanskrit: śaṃ no devīr abhiṣṭaya āpo bhavantu pītaye | śaṃ yor abhi sravantu naḥ ||
english: May the divine Waters be auspicious to us for our succour, auspicious for us to drink; may they flow about us bringing well-being and ease.

sanskrit: āpaḥ pṛṇīta bheṣajaṃ varūthaṃ tanve mama | jyok ca sūryaṃ dṛśe ||
english: O Waters, fill me full of healing medicine, a shelter for my body; and may I long behold the sun.

sanskrit: apsu me somo abravīd antar viśvāni bheṣajā | agniṃ ca viśvaśaṃbhuvam ||
english: Soma declared to me that within the Waters are all remedies, and Agni who brings well-being to all.

sanskrit: īśānā vāryāṇāṃ kṣayantīś carṣaṇīnām | apo yācāmi bheṣajam ||
english: Ruling over precious things, dwelling among the peoples — from the Waters I beg healing medicine.

sanskrit: ambayo yanty adhvabhir jāmayo adhvarīyatām | pṛñcatīr madhunā payaḥ ||
english: The mothers — kinswomen who minister at the sacrifice — travel along their paths, mingling the milk with honey.

sanskrit: amūr yā upa sūrye yābhir vā sūryaḥ saha | tā no hinvantv adhvaram ||
english: Those yonder that are near the sun, and those with whom the sun moves together — may they speed our sacrifice.

sanskrit: apo devīr upa bruve yatra gāvaḥ pibanti naḥ | sindhubhyaḥ kartvaṃ haviḥ ||
english: I call upon the divine Waters where our cows drink; an oblation is to be made to the rivers.

sanskrit: apsv antar amṛtam apsu bheṣajam | apām uta praśastiṣv aśvā bhavatha vājinaḥ ||
english: Within the Waters is immortality, within the Waters is medicine; and in the praises of the Waters, O horses, you become vigorous steeds.

sanskrit: vidmā śarasya pitaraṃ parjanyaṃ bhūridhāyasam | vidmo hy asya mātaraṃ pṛthivīṃ viśvadhāyasam ||
english: We know the father of the arrow — Parjanya, of many sustaining powers; we know indeed its mother — Pṛthivī, sustainer of all.

sanskrit: jyāyake pari ṇo nama- -aśmā bhavatu nas tanūḥ | viruḍvihi varīyo 'rātīr apa dveṣāṃsy ā kṛdhi ||
english: Homage around us to the bowstring; may our body become stone-hard. O plant, grow mightier — drive away hostilities, sweep off malevolences.

sanskrit: vṛkṣaṃ yad gāvaḥ pariṣasvajānā anasphuraṃ śaram arcanty ṛbhum | śaram asmad yāvaya didyum indra śaṃ no bhavantv apa oṣadhīr imāḥ ||
english: When the cows, embracing the tree, do reverence to the quiverless, unquivering, skillfully-wrought arrow — drive the shooting shaft away from us, O Indra; may these herbs be auspicious to us.

sanskrit: indrasya vajro apa hantu rakṣasa ārād visṛṣṭā iṣavaḥ patantv asmat ||
english: May Indra's vajra smite away the demon; may the arrows shot from afar fly away from us.
